claims.text: Ask: what they're proud of; what's exciting about this stage and what they like most about this age; how the family is doing; what they enjoy about the child; questions or concerns.
claims.quote: What are you most proud of since our last visit? (If the parent responds, “Nothing,” the clinician should be prepared with a compliment, such as, “You made time for this visit despite your busy schedule.”) • What’s exciting about this stage of development? What do you like most about this age? • How are things going in your family? • Let’s talk about some of the things you most enjoy about your child. • What questions or concerns do you have about your child?
claims.locator: 18 month visit, Health Supervision: History / Review of Systems

claims.text: Past medical hx: any specialty or emergency care since the last visit.
claims.quote: received any specialty or emergency care since the last visit?
claims.locator: 18 month visit, Health Supervision: History / Review of Systems

claims.text: Family hx: any new health condition or death in the family; if yes, who has or had it, age at onset and diagnosis, or age at death.
claims.quote: developed a new health condition or died? If the answer is Yes: Ascertain who in the family has or had the condition, and ask about the age of onset and diagnosis. If the person is no longer living, ask about the age at the time of death.
claims.locator: 18 month visit, Health Supervision: History / Review of Systems

claims.text: Social hx: major family changes or stressful events and their effect; what they find most difficult about the child.
claims.quote: What major changes have occurred in your family since your last visit? Tell me about any stressful events. What is the effect of these changes on your family? • What are some of the things you find most difficult about your child?
claims.locator: 18 month visit, Health Supervision: History / Review of Systems

claims.text: ROS — concerns about: head shape; crossed eyes; ears, nose and throat; breathing; vomiting or spitting, bowel movements; genitals or rectum; skin; development (muscle strength, movement of arms or legs, developmental concerns).
claims.quote: Do you have concern about your child’s • Head – Shape • Eyes – Cross-eyed • Ears, nose, and throat • Breathing • Stomach or abdomen – Vomiting or spitting – Bowel movements • Genitals or rectum • Skin • Development – Muscle strength, movement of arms or legs, any developmental concerns
